title: fix(scripts): floor the derived population in the engine-double and type-check gates
body:
Fixes #13014

Implements the audit's residual **R1** and nothing else. The card as filed proposed "an extractor that returns nothing must be an ERROR"; that is already the law in all four gates it named, and its flagship instance was misdiagnosed — the rebuttal is already in the tree at `scripts/check-stack-collection-maps.mjs:30-45`. Not implemented as written, per the re-scoping in the four-gate audit.

Clause-②: no
`scripts/**` only — no `packages/**` source and no published surface. Re-derived rather than copied: `node -e "import('./scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs')…"` prints today's register as `docs/adr/** · .claude/** · skills/** · AGENTS.md · CLAUDE.md`, and neither changed file is in it.

## What R1 actually was, per gate — the brief's premise held for one gate and not the other

The brief stated both gates "exit 0 when the scan collects nothing AND the ledger is empty". Measured, not assumed:

| gate | scan collects nothing + ledgers empty, BEFORE this PR | verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `check-type-check-coverage` | **exit 0**, prints `OK — 0/0 workspace packages type-checked` | premise HOLDS |
| `check-engine-double-contract` | **exit 1**, four named refusals (`DISCOVERED` x3 + `SEAMS_DISCOVERED`), ledger-independently | premise **FALSE** |

`DISCOVERED` and `SEAMS_DISCOVERED` are unconditional zero-floors on the derived population. So the engine gate's residual is narrower and different: a **partial** collapse, which no zero-check can see — and it is reachable by the remedy the gate's own error text prescribes.

**The engine gate's real blindness, measured end to end.** A tree carrying one package of eighty (`packages/mcp`) with all three ledgers emptied:

1. first run — exit 1, 17 findings, each ending *"Run `node scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write` and commit."*
2. doing exactly that, then re-running — **exit 0**, `check-engine-double-contract: OK — 15 pinned, 0 in the DEBT ledger, 0 exempt.`

15 pinned rows where the whole tree has 779, from a walk that read 26 test files where the whole tree has 3,503. Every verdict this gate reaches is a statement about the set discovery handed it.

**The type-check gate's blindness** is the brief's R1 verbatim. Its only guard is ledger reconciliation, and that guard is on a timer: `PHANTOM_PIN_DEBT` and `UNCHECKED_SOURCE_DEBT` are **already `{}`** on `854639b311` — the ratchet reached zero and took its share of the floor with it, as designed, with nothing anywhere saying so.

## The change

The `floorProblem()` shape from `check-dual-build-cjs-loads.mjs`, over the **DERIVED** population in each gate, plus a `provenanceLine` on every green run and a distinct exit code `2` for a refusal (a finding stays `1`; the type-check gate's prerequisite stays `3`).

⛔ No floor is over a ledger. A ledger floor would red the ratchet's own success, which is the defect and not the repair. The type-check gate asserts this mechanically rather than only in prose (`the census names only derived populations, never a ledger`).

**Measured on `854639b311` — every number, and how it was taken.** All eight come from running each gate with its floors installed and reading its own `provenance` line. Controls in the report; the two walk counts were each independently reproduced by a `find` pipeline to the exact integer, with a nonsense control returning 0.

| gate | population | measured | floor | headroom |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| engine | `testFiles` — the discovery walk | 3503 | 2800 | 20% |
| engine | `productionFiles` — the seam walk | 2596 | 2000 | 23% |
| engine | `discoveredFiles` — (file, verb) pairs parsed | 911 | 700 | 23% |
| engine | `pinnedRows` — the RETAINED census | 779 | 600 | 23% |
| type-check | `packages` — the workspace enumeration | 80 | 64 | 20% |
| type-check | `walkedTestFiles` — the per-package walk, tests | 3503 | 2800 | 20% |
| type-check | `walkedSourceFiles` — the same walk, sources | 2521 | 2000 | 21% |

Each row measures a different **stage**, not one number several times — walk, then parse, then guard-recognition on the engine side; enumeration, then each half of the per-package walk on the type-check side. Two considered omissions are recorded in the source rather than left silent: no floor on the engine gate's `seamCount` (population 6, any width would be invented), and none on the type-check gate's `covered` (already protected — if manifest reading broke, `COVERED` fires for every package in the same run).

## Acceptance evidence

| # | requirement | result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | before leg | measured above; **simulated**, not a blindness proof — the condition is not in the tree. How: fixture roots outside the worktree, with the gates' own scripts and empty scan roots. Reported honestly because the engine leg falsified the stated premise. |
| 2 | after: loud refusal; healthy tree unchanged | collapse trees now **exit 2** naming the fallen population. Healthy tree: **exit 0**, and the green text `diff`s **identical** to the pre-change run apart from the added `provenance` line. |
| 3 | negative control (mandatory) | engine: an unpinned engine double planted in `packages/mcp` — **exit 1**, three `PINNED` findings, **0** `REFUSES` lines. type-check: a new uncovered workspace package — **exit 1**, two findings, **0** `REFUSES` lines. Neither floor fires on a healthy tree. |
| 4 | honest message | each row's text names only its own stage. Asserted mechanically, both directions: a fallen `testFiles` row must match `discovery walk` and must **not** match `seam walk` or `RETAINED census`. |
| 5 | battery floors ratcheted to what runs | engine roster 31 to 32, new battery pinned at its measured **23** cases; type-check roster 61 to 62, new battery at its measured **23**. Both counts taken with a **firing** control (pin at 999, gate names the real number) and a **nonsense** control (each row asserted at its own floor, which must pass). |
| 6 | same shape or different? | **Different populations, same mechanism.** Details below. |

## Do the two gates want the same floor shape? (acceptance 6)

**The mechanism is identical; the populations are not, and neither is what they are protecting against.** Both use one frozen `MEASURED_POPULATION` record, sibling `MIN_` constants, a pure first-row-wins `populationFloorProblem`, a `populationProvenanceLine` on green, and exit `2`. But the engine gate floors *walk to parse to pin* over `packages/` + `examples/` recursively, and its gap is a **partial** collapse laundered through `--write`; the type-check gate floors *enumeration to walk* over the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` members, and its gap is a **total** collapse once the ledgers empty. Row counts differ (4 vs 3) and no row is shared.

⇒ **A shared helper is warranted**, and ⛔ it is deliberately **not** built here — that is a third card, per the brief. Worth noting for whoever takes it: the honest extraction is the row-walk plus the provenance formatting, parameterised by the row table; the row tables themselves must stay in their own gates, because each `why` is a claim about that gate's internals.

## Hazards — ⛔ this list is not complete

**Swept:** that neither floor reds on `origin/main` (both `=` on every provenance column); that no floor exceeds its own record (asserted in both self-tests); that the green text is otherwise byte-identical; that a real finding still reds with the floor silent, in both gates; control bytes in both files (gate plus an independent `grep -naP` sweep, both clean); the full derived gate family (33 of 33 accounted for by `dispatch-gates --ran`, 0 UNRUN); repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`, exit 0.

**One real finding my own change produced, and fixed:** `check:entry-guard` refuses a `scripts/**` file that exports a binding **and** runs on import. The precedent exports these two functions because it already guards its dispatch with `isEntrypoint`; retrofitting that to two large gates' argv handling is out of scope, and nothing imports them (the self-tests are in the same modules), so they are module-local and the rule no longer reaches either file. The reasoning is written beside each function so it is not re-added.

**NOT swept, and named:** `pnpm check:type-check-debt` exits **3 — `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`**, not a finding. It is the `--re-measure` path and needs a built workspace closure this container does not have. It reads no code path this diff touches. Declared to CI. I also did **not** audit either gate on any axis but this one — not their CI wiring, not their other invariants, not their remaining self-test coverage.

**Drift already visible:** `origin/main` advanced to `c43bac7048` (#17047) while this was in flight, adding one test file and one fixture. That moves the population by +1 and the provenance line will print `+1` instead of `=` — which is the design working, not a defect. The records stay pinned to `854639b311`, the commit they were actually taken on.

## Changeset

None. `scripts/` reaches 0 published manifests, so nothing published moves. If `Check Changeset` reds, ⛔ no label applied from here — reporting it for the PM to apply `skip-changeset`.
